The ITER converter and coil model was built in four days. In that time it gained a switched-circuit solver, every PF, CS and VS converter unit, a current controller per supply, nova's coupled coil, passive and plasma plant, and turn-resolved windings. About 120 merges landed, and 38 research pages record the studies. The lead presents the model in the week of 19 October 2026. What the audience needs is that each number shown was produced by the code at the presented revision. Each number must also be shown with its inputs, the evidence behind it and the size of its uncertainty.

Three things stand in the way, all found in the portfolio review of 17 October 2026:

  • No whole-suite run since 14 October. The last one passed 417 tests with 8 skipped, at revision 0626170. Every merge since has run a focused gate only, as the test protocol prescribes, so the merged head as a whole is unverified.
  • Pages that disagree. The controller page still says the CS coils, PF1, PF6 and VS3 miss the 1 % and 3 % tracking targets. Its later record says they meet them outside the switching-network windows. Its design table gives every supply a 25 dB gain margin, while the sampled-loop study finds VS1 unstable at the 2 ms control cycle. The averaged scenario loop therefore drives VS1 open-loop from DINA's recorded voltages.
  • No single record of what each result rests on. The bands that carry over from JT-60SA, the assumed inputs, and the gaps that remain sit in more than twenty places.

This plan builds no new physics. It verifies, records and reconciles what exists, and it writes the overview the presentation is drawn from. The integrated single-entry run of iter-switched-terminal-transients §6 stays with that plan. The overview states its status as it stands on the day.

§1 — The whole suite at the presented head

Run the whole suite once at the head of main, on compute, never on the login node: in place on the fleet allocation, where a worker already runs, or with srun --partition=all_debug --time=00:59:00 --cpus-per-task=4 --mem=32G from a login node. Cap the BLAS and XLA threads at 2 as the repository's instructions require, and write one log to /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/power_convertor/data/iter/gate-logs/suite-presented-head/suite.log, headed by the revision. Judge it by delta against the 14 October baseline held at data/iter/gate-logs/suite-py314-rerun/ (417 passed, 8 skipped at 0626170; its summary.json lists the skips): added failures, by test id. Attribute each added failure to the merge that introduced it. Its fix is a separate node, in a file nobody else holds, or is handed to the owning plan; this section runs and records and changes no source. If the suite runs longer than 20 minutes, record the slowest ten tests. A suite that has slowed is a robustness finding too. The suite is run again at the revision actually presented, since the head moves as the other S3 plans land.

Done when the log exists at the revision that ran and the record lists every added failure with its attribution, or none. The record is this section's landing evidence, docs/evidence/fragments/iter-integrated-model-assurance/suite-presented-head.html, headed by the revision; §2's register cites it as a row, so §1 and §2 write no file in common. A test that fails at the baseline revision and still fails is listed as pre-existing, not as added. That pre-existing list is the negative control that the delta is computed against the right base.

§2 — The claims register

One research page, docs/research/iter-model-claims-register.html, has one row per headline result, with:

  • the number and its unit;
  • its band: a low and a high value with the reason for each end (a JT-60SA band, an input range, a step-convergence spread), or the explicit entry "no band" with what is missing;
  • the inputs and their authority: IDM, a stated assumption, or DINA's demand, citing the section of the IDM register that records each one, its ratings tables for ordinary limits and its §8 inconsistency list by item number, rather than restating it;
  • the evidence it was validated on: a JT-60SA band, the Simscape cross-check, an analytic control, or none;
  • the open assumptions it depends on, by their IDM register §8 item number where one exists, so that the register and the IDM ledger stay one ledger;
  • the page and anchor it comes from.

Rows are ranked by uncertainty times consequence. The review seeds these rows, and the node adds every other headline it finds:

  • the switching-network insertion putting 13.05 kV across PF1 against its 12 kV envelope;
  • the PF1/PF6 pair asked for 1.8–2.0 % above its 2.1 kV rating in the limit windows;
  • CS3L's 18.5 % rms initiation deviation, traced to the 778SPD table;
  • VS1 run open-loop, and VS3's 3.45 dB gain margin;
  • the PF6 damped edge peaks of 3.61–3.62 kV against 2.5 kV;
  • the VS1 IGBT edge reaching about 2.2 kV across PF3 and PF5;
  • the 12–35 % of each pulse in which the whole-pulse ripple does not model the circulating bridges;
  • PF2's winding mode at 595 Hz beside the 600 Hz line;
  • VS3's open flux balance;
  • the JT-60SA bands the ripple results inherit. The 6f and 12f lines land within about 3 dB, 18f and above miss by 10–13 dB, and the inter-circuit harmonic coupling exceeds induction by about 1.9 times, unexplained. Transient pickup is validated within 4 % of the 5 ms-smoothed peak.

Done when every ITER study page under docs/research/ that carries a headline result, the seeded rows above included, has its headline numbers in the register, and the five highest-ranked rows are named at the top. The register states that page set at its head. Every evidence anchor is a link. A test, tests/test_claims_register.py, runs reckon audit-doc --check-links over docs/, whose link audit resolves in-page anchor ids, and fails on any dangling-anchor or dangling-link finding the audit reports for the register. The audit itself reports these at warn level and exits 0, so the test reads its findings, not its exit code. A copy of the register with one anchor broken on purpose fails the test.

§3 — The pages reconciled

Where two pages, or a page and the code, give different values for the same quantity, establish which is current and correct the other. Correct it in its owning page, with the earlier value kept and marked superseded. Redraw a figure through its own script only when its inputs have changed since it was drawn. The known cases:

  • the controller page's tracking and margin statements against its own later record and against the sampled-loop margins;
  • the reference scenario: 105052/1 in the controller and time-series pages against 105069/3, which the SRO selection names for the PF studies;
  • the whole-pulse ripple, drawn before the CS unit gained its circulating dual-converter mode on 17 October;
  • any figure drawn before the move to the 778SPD design values on 16 October.

Before writing, check every page against the live write claims. A page another node holds is left alone, and its owner is told what to correct.

Done when every case is corrected or handed off with the corrected value named, and every redrawn figure has been rendered and inspected, with that inspection recorded in the gate log. The register must also agree with the pages it cites: tests/test_claims_register.py also compares one pinned number per row against the cited page's text, and it fails when the page's number is edited on purpose.

§4 — The overview the presentation is drawn from

docs/research/iter-integrated-model-overview.html tells the model's story in the order an audience follows it:

  • what the model answers: whether the converters, switching networks, discharge units, grounding and busbars, as designed in IDM, can deliver DINA's coil currents within their ratings;
  • the plant, the converters, the controllers and the coupled coils;
  • what it finds, coil by coil, against the IDM ratings;
  • how far it is trusted, from JT-60SA and from the controls;
  • what remains open, and what the dummy-load recordings will test next.

It reuses existing figures by their project-absolute paths. It draws one new figure in docs/figures/iter-integrated-model-overview/: each supply's largest demanded voltage over the SRO cases against its rating, with the register's band. It reads the twelve SRO envelope cases' averaged-loop runs that scripts/iter/sro_scenario_selection.py already stores in data/iter/sro_scenario_selection/ (one run per case, with deliverability.json), taking each supply's largest applied voltage from them rather than running the cases again. The older six-case census of scripts/iter/scenario_loading.py is not the SRO set and is not used. The figure is drawn through power_convertor.figure_layout.save_figure in the repository's colour roles. Every number in the prose links to its register row.

Done when tests/test_claims_register.py passes over the overview too, finding no dangling anchor or link and no number in the overview's prose without a register row; every figure it shows has been rendered and inspected. Negative control: a copy of the overview with one number whose register row is removed fails the test. A reviewer renders the page's figures. Clipped, overlapping or unreadable labels are blocking.
